turns.text: Welcome to the interview.
Mm, sure — happy to be here. Go ahead whenever you're ready.
What time did you go to bed last night?
Around 2:30 in the morning, actually — later than I'd planned. Had a client's quarterly filing that wouldn't wrap itself up.
Approximately how many hours did you sleep last night? Would you say you slept well? Why or why not?

Probably around six hours, give it or take. I wouldn't say I slept "well" in the sense of it being deep and uninterrupted — I woke up twice to glance at my phone, which is a dumb habit I haven't kicked — but I felt reasonably okay by mid-morning. I've stopped expecting a perfect night's sleep, honestly, so "good enough" is my usual bar.
What was the last activity you engaged in before going to bed? Why did you choose to do that activity?

Reading paperback thrillers, actually, propped up with the fan running for noise. It's the closest thing I have to a wind-down ritual — beats staring at another screen after a full day of spreadsheets.
That does sound like a nice ritual. Do you remember the title or author of the thriller you were reading last night, or what it was about?
Yeah — it was one of the Jack Reacher ones, honestly can't remember which, they kind of blur together at this point. Something about him getting mixed up in a small-town conspiracy, standard stuff.

Thanks for explaining that. 

What factors have most affected your sleep quality over the past two weeks?

Factors have most affected my sleep quality over the past two weeks? Honestly, the biggest one is just workload spikes — quarterly filing crunch pushes my bedtime back by an hour or two some nights, and that throws off the routine even if I still wake up around the same time. Otherwise not much has changed — same fan, same no-caffeine-after-3-rule, nothing dramatic.
Is this pretty typical for you, or has something changed recently with your workload or sleep, compared to a few months ago?

Pretty typical, yeah. This has basically been my rhythm for a couple years now — the late nights, the natural wake-up. The only thing that shifts is the intensity around filing deadlines, and even that's just the same pattern turned up a notch, not something new.
Overall, are you happy with how you are sleeping these days? Why or why not?

Honestly, yeah, mostly. It's not textbook — I'm not getting eight hours by the clock most nights — but I wake up at a consistent time, I'm not dragging through the day, and I've made peace with the fact that my schedule runs later than everyone else's. If I weren't happy with it I'd probably have changed something by now instead of just working around the fan and the paperbacks.
You’ve probably heard the advice that adults should get 7–9 hours of sleep a night. Does that feel practical for you right now?

Honestly, not really — not consistently, anyway. I probably hit that on a slow week, but with my hours I'm usually closer to six and a half, seven. I've made peace with it though, since the wake time staying steady seems to matter more to how I actually feel than hitting some number on a chart.
What makes it easy or difficult for you to actually get that much sleep?

Sleep's easy for me because nobody's waiting on me in the morning — no kids, no partner, no boss with a start time — so I just let the schedule fall where it wants. The hard part's really just self-inflicted: I'm the one setting client deadlines, and when I stack them badly the late nights creep even later.

Thanks for explaining that.

Many people check their mobile phones, tablets, or computers right before bed. Do you do this, too? Why or why not?

Yeah, guilty as charged, though not right at bedtime — I'm usually reading a paperback to wind down instead. Where it gets me is overnight, if I stir I'll grab the phone out of habit just to check the time or see if a client emailed, which is probably not doing me any favors but it's a hard habit to break after years of running my own thing.
Do you regularly use social media? If yes, how do you typically use it, especially in the hours before bed?

Not really, no — I'll scroll through it during the day sometimes, but I'm pretty deliberate about keeping it out of the bedtime routine. Paperback wins over the phone at night, mostly because doomscrolling is a worse way to wind down than a cheap thriller.
Now a couple of quick questions about technology in general: Do you regularly use AI chatbots (such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, or similar applications)?
Not really, no — I'll poke at one occasionally if I need to draft a client email or double-check some tax wording, but it's not part of my routine, and definitely nowhere near bedtime.

Since you don’t really use social media or AI chatbots regularly, we can skip ahead.

If you could improve one thing about your sleeping habits, what would it be?

I'd trim the deadline stacking — space out client filings better so the late nights don't cascade like last night's. The wake time's already solid; it's really just not letting my own scheduling turn one late night into three.

Thanks for sharing that.

Now a few quick background questions. Feel free to skip anything you’d rather not share.

What is your age?
Thank you. What is your profession?
I run a small independent bookkeeping practice — mostly solo, working with local clients, out of my apartment.
Thank you. What is your country of birth?
United States.
Thank you. What is your current country of residence?
United States.

Thank you. That’s all the main questions I had.

Before we wrap up, is there anything else about your sleep or nightly routine that you’d like to add that we haven’t talked about?
